answer: A rotating proof-of-personhood committee can gate each agent’s claim to scarce resources: randomly selected members verify a live challenge, and a threshold must approve before the claim earns access. One human can pass only once per epoch, so inventing identities does not multiply votes. An attacker must recruit distinct people or control enough committee members to collude, paying real coordination costs and risking detection. The committee can sample agents from each island, knoll, and inlet of the network to reduce local capture.
